ops.title: Apple's on-device backend is 8x faster for the small tier and disagrees materially with Claude on structured verdicts
ops.body:
Measured 2026-09-18 while taking spawnllm's `sdk` extra (#125). `AppleBackend` is
already `BackendReady` on this machine and its `auto_select_tiers` is
`frozenset({"small"})`, so it is auto-selectable for exactly the tier
`ctx.call_llm` defaults to. It is simply last in spawnllm's `PRIORITY`. Promoting
it looked like a large free win and is not one.

Latency, same structured call, same process:

- apple 0.62s median (0.22s probe), codex 3.22s, claude-sdk 4.95s, claude CLI 5.11s.
- On the real (much larger) prompts: apple 3.26s median vs claude 25.05s.

Verdict quality, against the real prompts that would have been rerouted:

- cc-notes `SurfacePick` (12 real records, 4 touched files): mean Jaccard 0.29.
  Apple dropped 12 records Claude kept. That is the wrong direction — the
  filter's own system prompt says to bias hard toward surfacing because a
  missing record costs more than an extra line. Worst case dropped 7 of 9.
- cc-notes `RecordVerdict` router, 3 real writes: 0/3 agreement. On plain code
  both correctly declined to record, but apple returned `kind="task"` alongside
  `record=False`, which the schema's own contract forbids. That reads as weak
  prompt-following rather than different judgement.

So the swap was not shipped. Blast radius, if it is ever revisited: only
`specialty="general"` + `model="small"` — cc-notes' SurfacePick, RecordVerdict and
PlanTasks, and captain-hook's `prompt_check`. `llm_gate`/`llm_nudge` default to
`specialty="review"`, which promotes Codex to the front of the chain, so they are
unaffected either way. The routing change would belong in spawnllm's
`select_backend`/`PRIORITY` (the single owner of tier routing), never as a
captain-hook-side special case.

The win is real but needs a better small model or a tightened prompt, not this
backend.
